pr100.title: Announcements: V1 + redesign (audience fix, editor, scheduling, rich text, notify, engagement) (ORBIT-280)
pr100.body:
## Purpose and ticket

Announcements: admins of an office post announcements to their own people in Orbit (in-app and/or email), replacing the Team Portal slideshow for announcements. This is the V1 feature plus the redesign planned on 2026-10-15 (`docs/plans/2026-10-15-announcements-redesign.md`; decision log A1–A5, B1–B8, C1–C2, K1–K10).

## PR stage (choose one)

- [ ] **#1 Fork intake:** personal fork `<branch>` -> Moxie org **same-named** task branch (**developer self-review + manual merge; AI review optional**)
- [x] **#2 Staging:** Moxie org task branch -> Moxie org `staging` (**Raj review required**)
- [ ] **#3 Release:** Moxie org `staging` -> Moxie org `main` (list **all** included changes below)
- [ ] **Approved urgent production hotfix:** Moxie org fix branch -> `main`, with reviewed `main` -> `staging` sync
- [ ] Other (CadreAI mirror / Dependabot / legacy PR): explain

**Head repository + ref:** `Moxie-Pest-Control-Phoenix/moxie-portal:feature/announcements-v1` (@ `77afa95e`)
**Base repository + ref:** `Moxie-Pest-Control-Phoenix/moxie-portal:staging` (@ `d50d535e`)
**Earlier-stage PR(s) / reason for exception:** PR #1 = #99 (fork → org branch), merged.

**Scope check:** this PR contains only the announcements work. `staging` already has every `main` commit the branch merged in, so the diff against `staging` is exactly the feature's own 153 files (+17,733 / −212), the same as its diff against `main`. Every non-merge commit on the branch is an announcements commit. A test merge into `staging` is clean, and `0137` is free there (staging's highest is `0136`).

## Changes / implementation

- What this PR changes:
  - **Who sees it**: Everyone in this office, or Team / Role level / Location / Department plus people by name, read back as a sentence with a live count and a searchable "show who" list. Fixes the zero-recipient audience bug (D1/D2: people with no home branch).
  - **Editor**: one column (Content → Who sees it → When and how), preview in a slide-over panel using the real banner/modal/Center card/email, inline field errors, unsaved-changes guard, rich text (Tiptap: bold, italic, one heading, lists, links, up to 3 images), stop and publish times checked as they are entered.
  - **Categories**: Info, General, Urgent, Action Required (Important merged into Urgent).
  - **Scheduling**: publish now or at a date/time; the per-minute cron publishes due ones, requeues claims stuck > 15 min, and skips offices with the feature off.
  - **After publishing**: content and stop time stay editable (audience, delivery, publish time are frozen); "Notify people of this update" resets everyone's state and re-sends email once as "Updated: …".
  - **Engagement**: seen / opened / dismissed / done per person per notified version, cached totals, Mark as done for Action Required, and an engagement table on the record page for the owning office's admins.
  - **Navigation**: Announcements right after Dashboard with an unread badge; the floating bell is gone. Banners reuse the existing "awaiting your signature" notice (extracted as `NoticeBanner`).
  - **Admin list**: Drafts / Scheduled / Published / Retracted, audience sentence, row menu (Edit, Duplicate, Cancel schedule, Retract, Delete), Upload CSV shown disabled (B2). Loading and error states for every route.
- Any non-obvious design choices:
  - Message bodies are sanitized server-side with `sanitize-html` on every save (allowlist in `lib/announcements/html.ts`); the browser's HTML is never trusted. A plain-text copy (`body_text`) is stored for excerpts.
  - Images are private Vercel Blobs served only through `/api/announcements/images/view`, which checks the viewer is an admin of the owning office or a recipient, and that the image is listed on that announcement.
  - Delivery stays In-App / Email / Both (email-only kept) rather than an "Also email" checkbox.
  - Shared helpers extracted for reuse: `lib/media/downscale.ts` (old `lib/feedback/downscale.ts` re-exports it) and `lib/blob-errors.ts` (feedback attachments now use it; behaviour unchanged).
- Screenshots/video (for UI changes): not attached yet; the browser click-through is pending (see limitations).

## Test evidence (only check if actually passed)

- [x] Focused automated/regression tests (commands/results below)
- [x] `cd app && npm run check`
- [x] `cd app && npm run build`
- [ ] Applicable GitHub CI + security jobs passed on current base
- [ ] Deployed staging smoke test / acceptance scenarios (for staging signoff and release)
- [x] Checks skipped/blocked (explain)

**Commands, results and tested environments:**

- `npm run check` (typecheck + lint + Vitest): 253 files, all passing, 0 lint errors, on the head of this PR after merging `main` @ `1f2c9ab1` and renumbering the migration.
- `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true npm run build`: passes on the same head.
- `npm run test:db` (real SQL, local test database): 16 files / 117 tests passing, including the new `schedule.dbtest.ts` (two cron runs publish once; stop time first → back to draft; stuck claim requeued) and `notify.dbtest.ts` (archive-and-reset; cached counters equal `count(*)`). Run before the final `main` merge, which touched no announcement code.
- `npx tsx scripts/renumber-migrations.ts --check --base moxie/main`: "Migration numbers OK: 0137_announcements".
- GitHub CI + security: run on this PR; not yet passed at the time of opening.
- Skipped: browser checks for accessibility (axe), narrow widths and a two-office click-through were not done yet; they belong with the staging smoke test.

> Local test evidence is required for PR #1; secret scanning alone is not full CI.

## Risk / rollout / rollback

- [ ] No DB schema/data change
- [x] DB changes listed below, with migration IDs and **pre-/post-deploy order**
- [x] Auth/role/entity/office visibility affected
- [x] OAuth, secrets, external integrations, flags or deployment config affected

**Dependencies and config changes:**
- Migration `0137_announcements` (new tables `announcements`, `announcement_recipients`, `announcement_events`; seeds the `announcements` feature row on for every entity). Safe to apply **after** deploy: every table access sits behind the feature check, asserted by `release-guard.test.ts`; the cron does nothing until the feature rows exist.
- New dependencies: `@tiptap/react`, `@tiptap/core`, `@tiptap/pm`, `@tiptap/starter-kit`, `@tiptap/extension-link`, `@tiptap/extension-image`, `sanitize-html` (+ `@types/sanitize-html`).
- `vercel.json`: per-minute cron `/api/announcements/process` (bearer `CRON_SECRET`, on the middleware skip list).
- Env needed where used: `CRON_SECRET`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` (already used by feedback), `EMAIL_DEV_OVERRIDE` on staging. Each failing case answers a readable error.
- Visibility: admin routes are bounded to the admin's own entity (another office's id is a 404); recipient routes to the viewer's own snapshot row; writes refused under view-as.

**Known limitations / release blockers:**
- Browser checks (accessibility/axe, 1024/768 widths, click-through as a second office's admin and as a non-admin) still to do, on staging after it deploys.
- Staging runs no crons: scheduled publishing there has to be triggered by calling `/api/announcements/process` with the staging secret.
- Published announcements' image blobs are kept after retraction (no cleanup job yet).

**Rollback or roll-forward plan:** before 0137 is applied, a plain revert. After it is applied, keep the tables and turn the `announcements` feature row off per entity in the operator UI to hide everything; the cron is harmless with the feature off.

## Review and approval gates

- **PR #1 (fork -> org):** **I reviewed my own full diff**, checked test/build results and addressed or documented findings. An AI code reviewer (e.g. Greptile) is **optional**, not a formal GitHub approval. **I will manually merge** once satisfied; Raj/another developer is not required for this stage.
- **PR #2 (org -> staging):** **Raj must review and submit GitHub APPROVED** on the latest material changes, after current CI/security checks pass. PR #1 self-review or AI comments do not meet this gate.
- **PR #3 (staging -> main):** release owner confirms deployed staging testing, release contents and risks; current `main` ruleset requires **one eligible GitHub approval from someone other than the PR author** before a human merges.

Staging QA on deploy: run `0137` (staging applies migrations on push), set `CRON_SECRET`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`, `EMAIL_DEV_OVERRIDE`; trigger scheduled publishing by calling `/api/announcements/process` with the staging secret (staging runs no crons).

pr171.title: feat(feedback): ORBIT-493 Portal Feedback update into staging – tickets v2, follow-ups, API/MCP, GitHub and ClickUp sync
pr171.body:
## Purpose and ticket

**ORBIT-493.** Turns Portal Feedback into the Orbit team's ticket tracker and connects it to the tools around it. It covers:
- real ticket pages with collaboration and reviews;
- a reporter workspace (My Feedback);
- severity, work order and Plan my queue;
- subtasks, story points and Jira-style ticket flows;
- read-only API tokens and an MCP endpoint (ORBIT-479);
- GitHub sync for the Development panel;
- ClickUp sync.

This replaces #144, which GitHub closed when the org branch was renamed from `feature/portal-feedback-update` to `feature/orbit-493-portal-feedback-update` to carry the ticket. #144 had no reviews; its one comment was the Vercel bot.

## PR stage

- [x] **#2 Staging:** `Moxie-Pest-Control-Phoenix/moxie-portal:feature/orbit-493-portal-feedback-update` -> `Moxie-Pest-Control-Phoenix/moxie-portal:staging` (Raj's review required)

**Head:** `Moxie-Pest-Control-Phoenix/moxie-portal:feature/orbit-493-portal-feedback-update` @ `c178b8aa`
**Base:** `Moxie-Pest-Control-Phoenix/moxie-portal:staging` @ `5da8d80b`

**Earlier-stage PRs** (fork -> this org branch, all merged):

| PR | Merged | What it added |
|---|---|---|
| #142 | 2026-10-22 | Tickets v2: ticket pages, collaboration, tracker |
| #152 | 2026-10-26 | Migration renumber to 0141; participants |
| #165 | 2026-10-29 | Follow-ups: My Feedback, severity, work order, Plan my queue, subtasks, story points, ticket flows, guide |
| #166 | 2026-10-29 | ORBIT-479: read-only API tokens and MCP |
| #167 | 2026-10-29 | GitHub sync for the Development panel |
| #168 | 2026-10-29 | ClickUp sync |

**Scope check:** `git log moxie/staging..moxie/feature/orbit-493-portal-feedback-update` lists only this work: 128 commits, all by Vignesh, plus the PR #1 merges and the merges between the stacked branches. Nothing from other tasks is included. Main's one commit not on staging (`79640a51`, the #169 sync) is not in this branch.

**Diff against staging** (three-dot): 332 files, +43,291 / −1,713. It is the same set against main. The merge simulation into staging is clean.

**Workflow note:** this is one combined PR #2 for four stacked layers rather than four PR #2s. The layers were reviewed and merged one at a time as #165–#168. The per-layer walkthroughs can be shared on request.

## Changes

**Tickets and tracker** (#142, #152)
- Ticket pages for the team (`/admin/feedback/ORBIT-n`) and for reporters (`/feedback/ORBIT-n`).
- Ticket model: types, 11 statuses, module and affected page; bug context (steps to reproduce, expected and actual behaviour).
- Collaboration: markdown comments and internal notes, @mentions, watchers, attachments.
- Linking: references, relationships (blocks, is blocked by, duplicates, related), releases.
- Product reviews.
- Tracker:
  - filters and saved views;
  - resizable, reorderable columns;
  - tags and CSV export.

**Follow-ups** (#165)
- **My Feedback** (`/feedback`): a reporter, reviewer or participant sees only tickets they can read.
  - History shows the assignee, who changed the status and every assignee change, by name and never by email.
  - Back links retrace the tickets you came through.
- **Severity, reported severity and work order:**
  - **Plan my queue:** drag tickets to rank them, including between severities. Only ranked tickets get a Queue #.
  - Legacy priority is kept read-only.
  - A one-off backfill sets severity from priority. It never sets Critical.
- **Subtasks:** Task only. A subtask's reporter is whoever created it.
- **Story points:** Fibonacci scale, plus "?".
- **Ticket flows by type**, a Jira-style ticket guide, and type icons.
- **Sharing:** a tech user can share a ticket with someone by @mentioning them in a shared comment. The rules are in the access section of the guide.
- **Guide:** `docs/portal-feedback/README.md`, for users and developers, including access rules and a checklist for changing them. `docs/` is now tracked, including a new `docs/decisions/`.

**API and MCP** (#166, ORBIT-479)
- Per-user read-only bearer tokens, at My API tokens.
- Four GET routes under `/api/feedback/v1` and an MCP endpoint.
- A token sees exactly what its owner sees.
- The middleware lets token requests through only for those routes, and only while `FEEDBACK_API_TOKENS_ENABLED=true`. **Off by default.**

**GitHub** (#167)
- The Development panel lists branches, PRs and commits, matched to tickets.
- Hourly cron `/api/feedback/github/cron`. It is inert without `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Optional Vercel preview links, off by default.

**ClickUp** (#168)
- Links tickets to tasks in the "Orbit Projects" List.
- Daily cron `/api/integrations/clickup/cron`.
- Webhook route.
- With `CLICKUP_API_TOKEN` unset, ClickUp is off and its buttons are hidden.
- Writes need `CLICKUP_SYNC_WRITES=on` and webhooks need `CLICKUP_WEBHOOKS=on`. **Both off by default.**

**Dependencies:** `marked` ^15.0.12, `@dnd-kit/core` 6.3.1, `@dnd-kit/sortable` 10.0.0, `@dnd-kit/utilities` 3.2.2, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1.

**Config:** two new cron entries in `vercel.json`. New env vars are listed under Risk.

## Test evidence

On the head tree (identical to `c178b8aa`), 2026-10-29:
- `npm run check`: exit 0. Typecheck clean; lint 0 errors (26 warnings, all in files outside this PR); Vitest 306 files / 4,135 tests passed.
- `npm run build`: compiled successfully.
- `npm run test:db` (full suite): 297 / 298 passed. The one failure, `role-templates/copy.dbtest.ts` ("rolls the whole copy back…"), also fails on main and is unrelated to feedback.
- CI on this PR: see the checks below (not run before opening).

Run on each layer before it merged:
- Unit tests: 3,893 on #165 and 4,135 on #168.
- Feedback DB tests: 128 on #165 and 210 on #168.

Manual browser checks:
- The tracker, ticket pages, My Feedback and the Back trail were checked on a local dev server by the author while building.
- Not yet done in the browser: Plan my queue drag across severities, and the new History lines. They are covered by tests only.

## How to test

**Setup:**
1. Apply migrations `0141`–`0153` to the staging database before the deploy (see Risk).
2. Put a tech tester's email in `FEEDBACK_VIEWERS` and give them the app role `admin`.
3. Use a second, non-tech user as the reporter.
4. Leave every integration flag off.

**Dev tests:**
1. As the reporter, send feedback with the floating button. Open My Feedback: the ticket is listed and opens at `/feedback/ORBIT-n`.
2. As tech, open the ticket in Portal Feedback. Set severity, assign yourself, move it to In Progress, and post a shared comment. As the reporter, check:
   - the header says "assigned to <name>";
   - History lists the status and assignee changes with names;
   - the shared comment shows, and internal notes don't.
3. As tech, add a subtask:
   - it opens with "Back to ORBIT-n";
   - the reporter doesn't see it in My Feedback.
4. As tech, mention a third user in a **shared** comment, using the picker hint "No access yet: mentioning shares this ticket". That user can now open the ticket.
5. As the assignee, open **Plan my queue** and drag a ticket into another severity. Its severity changes and the move is in History.
6. Confirm the integrations are inert with their flags off:
   - My API tokens is not linked;
   - the ClickUp buttons are hidden;
   - the Development panel shows no GitHub data.

**Ready for staging** (check each before approving):
- [ ] Migrations 0141–0153 applied to staging; existing tickets open and keep their data
- [ ] Reporter sees only their tickets and shared content; tech sees everything
- [ ] Severity, work order and Plan my queue behave as described
- [ ] Integration flags off; the API, GitHub and ClickUp routes are inert

## Risk, rollout, rollback

**Database:** 11 migrations. Numbers were checked against both main and staging, whose highest is `0138`.

| Migration | What it does |
|---|---|
| `0141_portal_feedback_update` | Tickets v2 base columns and tables |
| `0142_portal_feedback_participants` | Participant grants; columns on references |
| `0144_feedback_work_order` | Reported severity and work order |
| `0146_feedback_work_order_unique` | Normalises ranks, then adds a unique index |
| `0147_feedback_subtasks` | `parent_id` |
| `0148_feedback_story_points` | `story_points` |
| `0149_feedback_severity_backfill` | **Data only:** severity from priority; never Critical |
| `0150_feedback_api_tokens` | API tokens |
| `0151_feedback_github_development` | GitHub commits and branch heads |
| `0152_feedback_clickup_links` | ClickUp links |
| `0153_feedback_clickup_sync_runs` | ClickUp sync ledgers |

- Apply all of them **before** the deploy: the code reads the new columns immediately.
- They are additive, and each file's header gives its rollback.
- `0141` widens `portal_feedback.status` and `portal_feedback.type` to varchar(40).
- `0149` changes existing rows. Its rollback is in the file header.

**Auth and access:**
- Ticket reads go through one access rule, in `access.ts` and its SQL twin. The levels are tech, reviewer, reporter, participant and none.
- `middleware.ts` gates bearer tokens to the v1 routes and MCP.
- `people-models.ts` registers the new profile foreign keys.
- Watching never grants access. A mention grants access only when a tech user writes it in a shared comment.

**Email:**
- The new-submission email template changed.
- The existing email to the reporter when their ticket is finished is unchanged.
- No mention, watcher or review emails.

**New env vars, all optional and off or empty by default:**
- Allow-lists: `FEEDBACK_ADMINS`, `FEEDBACK_COMMENT_MODERATORS`, `FEEDBACK_WATCHER_MANAGERS`.
- API: `FEEDBACK_API_TOKENS_ENABLED`.
- GitHub: `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `FEEDBACK_GITHUB_REPOS`.
- Vercel previews: `VERCEL_PREVIEW_LINKS`, `VERCEL_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_PREVIEW_PROJECT_ID`, `VERCEL_PREVIEW_TEAM_ID`.
- ClickUp: `CLICKUP_API_TOKEN`, `CLICKUP_LIST_ID`, `CLICKUP_SYNC_WRITES`, `CLICKUP_WEBHOOKS`, `CLICKUP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

**Integrations on first deploy:** leave all of them off. Enabling them later needs:
- a separate read-only GitHub token;
- a dedicated ClickUp service user scoped to the List;
- the product owner's yes for API tokens or ClickUp writes.

**Rollback:** revert the merge commit. The tables and columns are additive and can stay. Reverting the `0149` severity backfill is optional and is described in its file.

## Review and approval

Raj: please review and submit an approving review on the latest commit. A human merges after approval and green checks.

pr129.title: feat(field-ops): show collection rate beside reservice
pr129.body:
## Purpose and ticket

Field Operations now shows each field expert's **collection rate** (from Power BI, the same figure as the rankings tab of the field report) right beside **Reservice**. Requested to put collection rate next to reservice rate on the Field Ops screen. No ORBIT ticket; spec v0.3 is kept in the private feature folder.

## PR stage (choose one)

- [ ] **#1 Fork intake:** personal fork `feature/field-ops-collection-rate` -> Moxie org **same-named** task branch (**developer self-review + manual merge; AI review optional**)
- [x] **#2 Staging:** Moxie org task branch -> Moxie org `staging` (**Raj review required**)
- [ ] **#3 Release:** Moxie org `staging` -> Moxie org `main` (list **all** included changes below)
- [ ] **Approved urgent production hotfix:** Moxie org fix branch -> `main`, with reviewed `main` -> `staging` sync
- [ ] Other (CadreAI mirror / Dependabot / legacy PR): explain

**Head repository + ref:** `Moxie-Pest-Control-Phoenix/moxie-portal:feature/field-ops-collection-rate` (@ `126287b0`)
**Base repository + ref:** `Moxie-Pest-Control-Phoenix/moxie-portal:staging` (@ `60fe7198`)
**Earlier-stage PR(s) / reason for exception:** PR #1 = #108 (fork → org branch), merged.

**Scope check:** this PR contains only the collection-rate work. The branch was created from `main` `1f2c9ab1`, which `staging` already contains, so the diff against `staging` is exactly the feature's own 11 files (+1,091 / −6), the same as its diff against `main`. `git log moxie/staging..feature/field-ops-collection-rate` lists only the 6 collection-rate commits plus the #108 merge.

**⚠️ Draft: merge conflicts with `staging` to resolve before review.** Since this branch was cut, `staging` gained the Field Ops damage list (#128), which touches the same two files:
- `app/src/lib/actions/field-dashboard.ts`: both add imports at the same spot (keep both).
- `app/src/components/dashboard/field-stats-strip.test.tsx`: both branches created this test file; combine the two sets of tests, and staging's sample stats need the new `overallCollection` field.

Checks will be re-run against `staging` after the conflicts are resolved; this moves out of draft only then.

## Changes / implementation

- What this PR changes:
  - "Collection" beside "Reservice" in three places: each person's row, the top Reservice tile on the Field Ops landing page (Wallet icon + help text), and supervisor cards. Team lead cards and the "Avg Reservice" strip are unchanged.
  - New `app/src/lib/queries/field-collection-rate.ts`: live, read-only DAX read of `[Field Collections Rate | Non-NS/Starts]` from the Corporate Standard model, per `DimEmployee[email]`, for the header month, filtered to offices with `operationalStage` New or Veteran (the report's filter). Blank stays `null` ("—"); a real 0 shows "0.0%".
  - `fetchFieldDashboardData`: reads it alongside the existing Fabric reads, behind the existing 30-min page cache (key bumped v3 → v4). Current month only: if nobody on screen has a figure yet, falls back to the latest earlier month (≤12 back) for everyone, like reservice. Team figures are a simple average of people (same as Reservice beside them). Power BI's own report total instead recalculates the rate over everyone's combined numbers (bigger books count for more), so Orbit's team/overall Collection will not equal the report total even for the same people — see Known limitations.
  - Each Power BI read is time-limited to 8 s (16 s worst case on fallback days); on timeout/failure the figure is "—" and the page still renders. A warning is logged when Power BI returns no figures at all.
- Any non-obvious design choices:
  - **Display only:** no `metric_catalog` row, no snapshot storage, no role template/scorecard change, no effect on grades, status colours, warnings or attention items.
  - Only the viewer's office's field staff values reach the payload/cache; emails never leave the server.
  - Same email matching as reservice: anyone whose email has a figure in that model shows it, others "—".
- Screenshots/video (for UI changes): not captured; checked on a local server (2026-10-19) against live Power BI, see Test evidence. To check on staging.

## Test evidence (only check if actually passed)

- [x] Focused automated/regression tests (commands/results below)
- [x] `cd app && npm run check`
- [ ] `cd app && npm run build`
- [ ] Applicable GitHub CI + security jobs passed on current base
- [ ] Deployed staging smoke test / acceptance scenarios (for staging signoff and release)
- [x] Checks skipped/blocked (explain)

**Commands, results and tested environments:** local worktree on macOS, HEAD f81965ea (results from PR #1; to be re-run against `staging` after the conflict fix).
- `npx vitest run src/lib/queries/field-collection-rate.test.ts` → 44/44 pass (plus component tests for the three places: field-expert-card, field-stats-strip, supervisor-card).
- `cd app && npm run check` → pass (225 files, 3044 tests; typecheck clean; lint 0 errors, pre-existing warnings only).
- `cd app && npm run build` → fails locally only at "Collecting page data" on missing env vars (worktree has no env file). `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true npm run build` → **pass**.
- **Live Power BI comparison (2026-10-19, local server, "Arizona Operations" view, October):** compared with the Field Care Report filtered to Owner Austin Clark / Office Phoenix / 10/1–10/19 (report total 12.73%). Every person matched by email has the **same per-person rate** as the report, to the hundredth (e.g. Gavin Milius 47.93, Bradon Moore 45.79, Gabriel Romero 42.36, Tyler Kiel 3.18, and 12 people at 0.00 in both), so the measure name and office filter are confirmed. The overall figure differs (Orbit 9.75% vs report 12.73%) for the reasons under Known limitations. Read-only DAX queries plus the local snapshot DB; nothing written.
- No DB tests (none needed: no DB change).

> PR #2 needs current CI/security checks on the `staging` base before Raj's approval.

## Risk / rollout / rollback

- [x] No DB schema/data change
- [ ] DB changes listed below, with migration IDs and **pre-/post-deploy order**
- [ ] Auth/role/entity/office visibility affected
- [x] OAuth, secrets, external integrations, flags or deployment config affected — reuses the existing Power BI service login (`FABRIC_AAD_*`) and Corporate Standard model; no new secrets or config.

**Dependencies and config changes:** none.
**Known limitations / release blockers:**
- **On staging, if every Collection figure shows "—", treat it as broken** (wrong measure name or office-stage value), not "no data yet"; check logs for `[field-collection-rate] Power BI returned no collection figures`. Compare a few January 2026 people with the rankings export.
- **Orbit's overall/team Collection will not match the Power BI report total, and that is expected.** Worked example (October, Arizona Operations vs report filtered to Phoenix): report **12.73%**, Orbit **9.75%**. The gap is fully accounted for by:
  1. **Different people:** Orbit's "Arizona Operations" view covers Phoenix + Tucson; the report was filtered to Phoenix (Austin Clark owns only Phoenix in Power BI). Orbit counts 7 Tucson people with figures, and Tucson runs lower this month (8.91% on Power BI's own total).
  2. **People Orbit can't match by email** (a data issue, not code): Trace (Marlin) Brewer, 50.59% in Power BI, has a different email in Orbit than in Power BI so shows "—"; Michael Gonzalez, 3.35%, has a placeholder Paylocity email in Orbit; Jackson Barber, 0%, is not in Orbit (local DB is a snapshot, so check production before fixing).
  3. **Different totalling:** Orbit takes a simple average of each person's rate; Power BI recalculates over the combined numbers. Same 28 Phoenix people: simple average 11.82% vs report 12.73%. Orbit's own 46 people on Power BI's totalling would be 12.01%.

- **Actions** (`lib/actions/talent-rating-freeze.ts`): one read action plus Freeze now, Schedule/Move, Cancel and Unfreeze. Every write checks `requireRole('admin')` + `isEntityAdmin` and is refused while viewing as someone. The office always comes from the signed-in user, never the client. - **Non-obvious choices:**
  - No cron. A month counts as frozen once `freeze_at <= now()`, worked out on the server.
  - `requireLead`/`requireRaterView` moved verbatim into a plain module so they aren't callable endpoints.

- Focused tests: freeze helpers, save guard, freeze actions, freeze timer (10), notice markup pin, banners; DB test `src/test/talents/freeze.dbtest.ts` 10/10 on a local test DB (includes a freeze starting between two saves).

**Setup:** branch `feature/talent-ratings-freeze` (or staging after merge) with migration `0140_talent_rating_freezes` applied; an admin, a lead and an evaluator; for office checks, the second-office seed (`app/scripts/seed-test-entity.sql`, local only).

1. As a lead, open Forms → Team Talent Ratings: there's no Freeze ratings control.
2. As an admin, click Freeze now and confirm: the badge says Frozen.
3. As a lead, open that month: amber banner, scores and Submit disabled.
4. As the admin, try to save on the frozen month: it's locked, with "Unfreeze it to make changes."

pr220.title: Store recruiting queue calls (ORBIT-503)
pr220.body:
Calls on TalkDesk's recruiting queue matched no routing rule and were dropped as no_department before a row was written. Delaney Byrd shows 664 October calls on Productivity and almost none in Calls logs.

- New `recruiting` pipeline config: AI summary only, no scoring, FieldRoutes notes off. The prompt keeps medical, pay, background-check and ID details out of the summary.
- `keepOwnScoring` lets a config opt out of the office observation rubric that `getPipelineConfigs()` applies to every department, so a re-seed cannot put candidate calls on the customer rubric.
- `QUEUE_MAPPING`: recruiting maps to Recruiting. This is the routing fallback, and it gives the Productivity queue groups a Recruiting group instead of Other queues.
- `scripts/setup-recruiting-calls.ts` (dry run by default) creates the `recruiting` department under the People Relations entity, a ring_group rule at priority 40 (after every existing rule) and the pipeline config. Run it after deploy: code first, data second.
- `scripts/backfill-recruiting-calls.ts` re-queues the 1,570 dropped recruiting calls since 9/1 in batches of 25, and only while the queue is nearly empty, so live customer calls stay first.

The department slug is `recruiting` rather than `people-relations` because `/calls/people-relations` is the People Relations team view and has no call-detail route; calls under that slug would link to a 404. Those calls still show in the People Relations team view, which lists the team's calls in any department.

Review fixes (second commit): the recruiting rule matches only calls that rang the queue, never by group membership, so People Relations attendance and az_peoplerelations calls stay out. The backfill releases each job once. Contacts labelled as candidates are not dropped as internal. Short calls stay unscored, and admins get a Recruiting tile.
